items.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Incredible. He – his room was so vast that at one point I started to feature him playing some of the classical things. People never expected to hear that. Those jive jazz musicians. I said, “Now he’s going to play an original piece by an Israeli composer, [Jabos Jacalalian?]” – whatever his name was. He played the heck out of that thing. Then he played something by Bach in B minor, and I fashioned it into – we went into a jazz thing. It was incredible what we did the second time out. He was one of the key people,…
I fortunately was – I was fortunate enough to have caught you with that configuration – I believe we talked about it yesterday – at Sweet Basil’s. You guys were pretty much there a lot.
